2. The facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in brief, are that respondent No. 1, Sonali Bank, as plaintiff, filed Money Suit No. 18 of 1985 against respondent Nos. 2-4 and the petitioner as defendant Nos. 1-4 for realisation of Taka 9, 34,500 with interest. The suit was later renumbered as Artha Rin No. 25 of 1990. The details of the Artha Rin suit are not relevant for the purposes of disposal of this Rule. During the pendency of the suit the petitioner filed a written statement denying the assertions and claims made in the plaint and also filed an application under Order I, rule 10(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) for striking off his name from the plaint as defendant No. 4, stating, inter alia, that in respect of the disputed remittance of Taka 8,42,000 in favour of the petitioner, which he claimed to have not received, he filed Money Suit No. 2 of 1981 in the Second Court of Subordinate Judge, Sylhet and same was decreed in his favour on contest against the opposite party No. 1 and that First Appeal No. 3 of 1984 later renumbered as First Appeal No. 680/91, challenging that decision is pending in the High Court Division. The petitioner claimed that since the present suit involves the self same matter, the suit cannot proceed against him and, as such, he is not a necessary party in the suit. The said application was allowed ex parte by order dated 20-7-1997 After about one year, on 22-6-1998, respondent No. 1 filed an application under Order XLVII, rule 1 of the Code for reviewing the earlier order dated 20-7-1997. The application of the respondent No. 1 was allowed by the impugned order. 

 5. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates, perused the petition and the affidavit in opposition clearly the decision reported in 46 DLR 292 is not applicable in the facts of the instant case since that case involved the review of a judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat, for which the Ain provides the right of appeal. We are of the view that since the Ain does not provide any remedy by way of review of an order of the Artha Rin Adalat, the provisions of Order XLVII, rule 1 will be amenable for the purposes of reviewing an earlier order of the Artha Rin Adalat. 

 6. The decision in the Sultana Jute Mills case is clear authority for the by now established principle that no writ or revision to the High Court Division will lie against any interlocutory order of the Artha Rin Adalat. Such avenue is clearly barred by section 6(1) of the Ain. Subject to the right of appeal under section 7 and application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code as provided by section 6(2) of the Ain, section 6 of the Ain bars the challenge of any proceeding, order, judgment or decree of the Artha Rin Adalat in any Court. But an inroad has been opened in respect of challenge against interlocutory orders before the Adalat itself. In the words of Mr Justice BB Roy Chowdhury "the word” কোন আদালত occurring in sub-section (1) of section 6 of the Act refers to any other court than the Artha Rin Adalat, the Islami Bank case reported in 52 DLR (AD) 76, cited above. In that case the Appellate Division reversed the decision of the High Court Division that the Adalat illegally assumed jurisdiction under Order IX, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure. We respectfully agree with the decision of the Appellate Division that the bar is not applicable to a party wishing to move an application under the provisions of the Code before the Artha Rin Adalat so long as the provision of the Code is not inconsistent with the provisions of the Ain. In the like manner as Mr Justice Kazi Ebadul Hoque did in the Islami Bank case, going through the provisions of the Ain we do not find any provision therein which is contrary to the provision of Order XLVII, rule 1 of the Code it is our considered view that an application before the Artha Rin Adalat is competent under Order XLVII, rule 1(1) (b) of the Code of Civil Procedure.
